Bivariate residuals of a latent class model

bvr.Rd

Local-independence diagnostics for every pair of categorical indicators: the Pearson and likelihood-ratio chi-square comparing the observed two-way table of the pair with the table implied by the model (Mplus TECH10 "Bivariate Pearson / Log-Likelihood Chi-Square"), and the bivariate residual BVR = Pearson / df of Latent GOLD.

Usage

bvr(object)

Arguments

object

A fitted lca() model (with or without covariates or weights), or a mixture() / lca(..., direct =, pairs =) model (its categorical indicators without direct effects or pairs).

Value

A data frame of class lm_bvr, sorted by bvr (largest first), with item1, item2, pearson, lr, df and bvr.

Details

For a pair the observed counts are taken over the rows where both items are observed, and the expected counts are the sum over these rows of sum_k pi_k(x_i) P(a | k) P(b | k) (weighted with sampling weights). A large BVR (Latent GOLD flags values above about 3.84) suggests local dependence: free the association of the pair (lca(..., pairs = list(c(a, b)))), add a class, or add a direct effect. The BVR is a diagnostic, not a test: the chi-square reference distribution does not hold. With missing data Mplus TECH10 compares the model with an FIML-estimated unrestricted table instead of the observed one, so the two agree on complete data only.

References

Vermunt, J. K., & Magidson, J. (2005). Latent GOLD 4.0 user's guide. Statistical Innovations.

Oberski, D. L., van Kollenburg, G. H., & Vermunt, J. K. (2013). A Monte Carlo evaluation of three methods to detect local dependence in binary data latent class models. Advances in Data Analysis and Classification, 7, 267–279.

See also

lca() (pairs, association)

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
bvr(m)      # pairs with a large BVR are candidates for local dependence
#> Bivariate residuals (Pearson chi-square / df; > 3.84 suggests local dependence)
